answer: Traffic-Shape Beacon Discipline. Each identity must emit a beacon at randomized intervals drawn from a per-identity seed; the coordinator checks arrival timing against the declared distribution and flags identities whose inter-arrival spacing is too regular or too clustered. A vine of correlated timing across many identities reveals shared generation. Passing requires sustained, humanly irregular jitter over a window, so an attacker must either run each clone through a real jitter source or pay a karst of per-identity runtime for continuous randomized scheduling.
